facts.text: Franklin Farm began as a 100‑acre dairy farm in 1936 when airline pilot James Franklin bought the land with $10,000 from an Irish Sweepstakes ticket.
By 1979 the Franklins expanded the property to 827 acres, making it one of Fairfax County’s largest dairy operations before development.
In 1980 the 827‑acre farm was subdivided into a master‑planned community of 1,777 homes across 27 neighborhoods, covering 1.32 square miles.
The community’s name honors its original owner, James Franklin, and reflects the area’s pastoral roots that still echo in its streets and parks.
Franklin Farm’s history dates back to at least 1798, when a historic house first appeared in Fairfax County tax rolls, marking early settlement.
The Franklin Farm Foundation, the homeowner association, governs the community and maintains its distinct character within the unincorporated CDP.
